title: ZenTrainer run spec, version 2
description: A training run: what to train and how. Each section has its own table below.

$schema.description: This schema's address, for editors: ignored.

spec_version.description: The spec's layout. An older one is brought up to date as it's read; a newer one (from a newer ZenTrainer) is refused.

seed.description: The run's seed: noise, shuffling and dropout.

kind.description: "checkpoint": one file with the model, text encoder and VAE (SD 1.5, SDXL). "split": separate files (Flux, Qwen Image, Z-Image, ...).

ckpt_name.description: checkpoint models: the file in ComfyUI's checkpoints folder.

unet_name.description: split models: the diffusion model, in diffusion_models.

unet_weight_dtype.description: How the diffusion model's weights load (ComfyUI's weight_dtype).

clip_name.description: split models: the text encoder, in text_encoders.

clip_type.description: split models: the text encoder's type, as ComfyUI's CLIPLoader names it (flux2, qwen_image, ...).

vae_name.description: split models: the VAE, in vae.

audio_vae_name.description: Joint audio-video models (MiniMax H3): their audio VAE, needed to train on a video's sound (dataset.video_audio) and for sound in samples.

folder.description: The dataset folder: pictures and videos with same-name caption files. A kohya-style "N_name" subfolder repeats its pictures N times.

resolution.description: Training resolution: pictures are resized to about this many pixels squared.

stages.description: Lower resolutions first: [{"resolution": 768, "until": 0.6}] trains at 768 for the first 60% of the run, then at `resolution`. Every resolution is cached before training. [] = one resolution throughout.

stage_blend.description: How much of the run each resolution change blends over, so nothing switches at once (0.6 to 0.8: the next resolution goes from no steps to every step).

buckets.description: Aspect-ratio buckets: each picture is resized to the closest shape of about resolution² pixels. Off = centre-cropped squares.

bucket_step.description: Bucket sides are multiples of this.

edit.description: Edit training: each picture's input picture(s) from `control_sets` are what the model edits from (as reference latents) and the caption is the instruction. For models that take reference images (Flux 3 Klein, Flux 2, Kontext, Qwen Image Edit, ...). Any control set turns it on.

control_sets.description: Control sets, in order: named folders of input pictures beside the dataset (_controls/<set>/<name>.<ext>; older <name>_control files are the "control" set). Several sets give each picture several inputs. Edit training with none uses "control".

edit_method.description: How the input picture joins the sequence: "" = the model's own way, or "index", "offset", "index_timestep_zero". "concat": channel inputs instead, each control set's picture (aligned with the target, the same size) as extra latent channels into a widened input layer, like ComfyUI's MOSS Image control adapters.

control_dropout.description: Channel inputs: the share of steps each input is left out (zeros), independently, so the adapter also works with some or none of them.

edit_template.description: Wraps each instruction: "{}" is the caption (e.g. a generalist edit model's own wording, for a specialist trained on top of it). "" = the caption as it is.

edit_grounded.description: The text encoder sees the input pictures too (Qwen3-VL based: Krea 2, Qwen Image): conditioning becomes per picture, encoded when the dataset caches.

disk_cache.description: Each picture's latents (and its own conditioning) in a file of its own, read when a step uses it: for datasets bigger than RAM (thousands of grounded edit pairs).

video_keyframes.description: MiniMax H3 image-to-video: each clip conditioned on its own first frame ("first") or first and last ("first_last"), as the fl2va model is at inference. "" = off.

caption_dropout.description: The share of steps that train on an empty caption.

caption_set.description: Which captions to train on: <name>.txt is "default", <name>.<set>.txt the others (tags, nl, ...).

caption_mix.description: Several caption sets to mix: each step picks one of the picture's at random. [] = caption_set only.

trigger.description: "[trigger]" in captions and sample prompts becomes this, and captions that don't mention it get it prepended ("ohwx, a photo of ...").

trigger_prepend.description: Prepend the trigger to captions that don't mention it.

masked_loss.description: Masked training: pictures with a mask only learn where it's white.

unmasked_weight.description: Masked training: how much the rest of the picture still trains (0 = not at all, 0.1 = lightly).

video_frames.description: Videos train as clips this many frames long at most (snapped to a length the model's VAE encodes exactly). An image model trains a video's frames as pictures.

video_fps.description: Clips resampled to this frame rate. 0 = the video's own.

video_mode.description: Which parts of a video become clips: "uniform" spread over it, "head" its start, "chunks" consecutive.

video_resolution.description: Each clip at about this many pixels squared (a clip costs frames x pixels, so videos usually train smaller than pictures).

video_audio.description: Train on each clip's soundtrack too (joint audio-video models with model.audio_vae_name), so cuts can learn the beat.

video_avoid_cuts.description: Keep clips inside one shot: no clip spans a hard cut. Off for edits where the cutting is the point (music videos).

video_stills.description: Each clip also trains its sharpest frame as a picture (with the clip's caption). Stills are never TREAD-routed and anchor the LoRA's detail.

alpha.description: The adapter's alpha. null = the rank (a scale of 1).

lora_dtype.description: What the adapter trains in. fp32: AdamW's steps on a LoRA are smaller than bf16 can represent at the weights' size, so most would round away. bf16 only with an optimizer that rounds stochastically (Automagic).

targets.description: Which layers get adapters: "attn" (attention projections), "mlp" (feed-forward), "attn_mlp" (both), "all" (every adaptable layer, like ComfyUI's native trainer), or a list of regexes over module names.

train_bias_norm.description: Train the biases and norm weights too.

init_from.description: A LoRA in the loras folder to continue from.

training_adapter.description: A LoRA applied while training only, never in samples or the saved file: e.g. a de-distillation adapter for a guidance-distilled model (MiniMax H3), so training sits on an undistilled base.

base_lora.description: A LoRA the trained one sits on everywhere (training, samples and use), e.g. a fix the model always needs. The saved LoRA leaves it out and records it: load it beside, at base_strength.

blocks.description: Only these transformer blocks get adapters, e.g. "20-49" or "10-": the backward stops at the first one, so steps are quicker, and earlier blocks stay untouched. "" = every block.

skip_blocks.description: These blocks get no adapters, e.g. "22" or "22, 30-31" (a block that skip-layer guidance skips stays the base's).

lr_scheduler.description: The learning rate over the run.

warmup_steps.description: Steps the learning rate ramps up over, from 0.

max_grad_norm.description: Gradients clipped to this norm. 0 = off.

lora_plus.description: LoRA+: the up matrices learn this many times faster than the down ones, which trains a LoRA faster for the same stability (paper: 16; 4 is a safe start). 0 or 1 = off.

ema.description: Weight averaging: checkpoints, samples and the saved LoRA use a running average of the adapter (0.98 = roughly the last 50 steps). 0 = off.

lr_floor.description: Automagic v3/v4: the adaptive rate never drops below this fraction of its start (v3's decays and can stall under-strength). 0 = no floor.

target.description: "native": each model's own prediction (noise for SD-style models, velocity for flow models). "x0": the loss on the denoised picture (ComfyUI's native trainer).

timesteps.description: How each step's noise level is drawn: "uniform"; "logit_normal" (AI Toolkit's "sigmoid"), shaped by logit_mean and logit_std; or "scheduler": the levels ComfyUI's scheduler `timestep_scheduler` samples at in `timestep_scheduler_steps` steps, each as often (trains where the LoRA will be used; few steps for a fast LoRA).

logit_mean.description: logit_normal's centre: positive leans to heavy noise (composition), negative to light (detail).

uniform_mix.description: logit_normal: the share of steps drawn uniformly instead, keeping a little training at the extremes it rarely visits (0.01).

shift.description: Flow-matching models: the training timestep shift. 0 = the model's own sampling shift, which favours heavy noise (composition, colour); a lower one (1-3) spends more steps on detail, such as faces.

bias.description: Lean the noise levels toward one end, whatever the distribution: "high_noise" for composition, layout and pose, "low_noise" for detail and texture (AI Toolkit's "content" and "style"). "balanced" = as drawn.

bias_power.description: How hard the bias leans: the draw to this power (3, as AI Toolkit, puts half the steps in the noisiest eighth for high_noise). 1 = not at all.

weighting.description: Per-noise-level loss weights. "flex" (flow models): AI Toolkit's "weighted", measured on Flex.1. "balance": measures the model as it trains and evens the pull of every noise level (EDM2's idea). "" = none.

spread.description: Noise levels from an even, low-discrepancy sequence instead of random draws: a small batch covers the schedule in a few steps, for a steadier loss.

training_dtype.description: The precision the model computes in.

gradient_checkpointing.description: Recompute activations in the backward instead of keeping them: much less VRAM, some speed.

grad_checkpoint_skip.description: Leave the last N blocks un-checkpointed: they keep their activations (more VRAM) and skip the recompute, the cheapest place to trade memory for speed.

offloading.description: Keep part of the model in RAM and stream it in: for models bigger than the card.

vram_headroom.description: With offloading: the VRAM kept free for activations, the LoRA and its optimizer (GB); the rest holds as much of the model as fits. 0 = auto (8 GB, more for long video clips).

tread.description: TREAD token routing on video steps (MiniMax H3): this share of a clip's tokens skips the middle blocks and rejoins unchanged (0.5 roughly halves their work). Stills, samples and validation always run whole. 0 = off.

tread_steps.description: The share of clip steps that route; the rest run whole. A dataset of clips only, routed every step, lets the LoRA learn to make up for the routing (over-sharpened samples): below 1 keeps whole steps.

int8_forward.description: int8 bases (MiniMax H3, Krea 2 int8): trained layers run ComfyUI's int8 kernel forward instead of a dequantized bf16 matmul. Off is slower: for comparing quality.

int8_backward.description: int8 bases: how the backward gets each frozen layer's input gradient. "w8a8": quantized to int8 too, on int8 tensor cores (about 2x the bf16 backward), for some gradient precision. "fused": a fused Triton kernel at full precision, without rebuilding the layer's bf16 weight. "bf16": the weight rebuilt in bf16 (ComfyUI's way; the slowest).

fp8_backward.description: fp8 bases: the backward's matmuls in fp8 too (ComfyUI's training_fp8_bwd). Faster, less precise.

compile_blocks.description: torch.compile the repeated transformer block, fusing the elementwise work around the matmuls; the first steps (and first sample) are slower while it compiles. "auto": on for runs long enough to repay that, when Triton is installed.

fused_qk_rope.description: Krea 2, MOSS, MiniMax H3: the attention's q/k norms and rope as one op with its own backward (Triton): the same maths, 6-9% a step. "auto": on while the blocks run uncompiled (compiled ones fuse these already).

bypass_mode.description: Adapters as forward hooks beside each layer instead of patched into its weight. Quantized bases always train this way.

attention.description: The attention backend while training (only ones with a backward pass; flash and sage have none).

likeness.description: Score each sample's face against the dataset's (with faces on for the dataset).

every.description: Sample every this many steps. 0 = off.

prompts.description: The samples: each a prompt, or {"prompt", "width", "height", "frames", "seed", "control"} with its own size, length, seed or (edit runs) picture to edit.

frames.description: Video models: frames per sample (1 = a still), snapped to a length the VAE decodes and saved as an .mp4 at fps.

sigmas.description: Custom sigmas, high to low (e.g. [1.0, 0.94, 0.85, 0.7, 0.5, 0.3, 0.12, 0]), in place of the scheduler and steps (len - 1 steps). [] = the scheduler.

seed.description: The first sample's seed; each next prompt the next one.

baseline.description: Render the prompts once before training: the base model's look, to compare against.

model_name.description: Sample with another model of the same family than the one training (e.g. train a raw model, preview on its turbo): a diffusion_models file for split models, a checkpoints file for checkpoint ones.

lora_strength.description: The trained LoRA's strength in samples.

turbo_lora.description: A turbo LoRA under every sample (not training, not the saved LoRA): few-step previews.

slg_mode.description: Skip-layer guidance, as ComfyUI's SkipLayerGuidanceDiT: "uncond" skips the layers in the negative pass only (no extra cost), "standard" adds a pass without them and pushes away from it by slg_scale.

slg_layers.description: Skip-layer guidance: the main (single-stream) blocks to skip.

slg_double_layers.description: Skip-layer guidance: double-stream blocks, for models that have them.

slg_scale.description: Skip-layer guidance "standard": how hard it pushes.

slg_start.description: Skip-layer guidance: where in sampling it starts (0 to 1).

slg_end.description: Skip-layer guidance: where it ends (0 to 1).

every.description: Measure every this many steps (and before training). 0 = off.

noise_levels.description: Noise levels each picture is measured at, spread over the schedule.

seed.description: Picks the pictures and their noise.

dataset.description: A held-out dataset folder to measure on instead, prepared like the training one (edit inputs, masks, captions): loss on pictures the LoRA never trains on, so the curve says whether it generalises rather than how well it fits. "" = pictures from the training dataset.

save_every.description: A checkpoint (the LoRA and its resume state) every this many steps. 0 = only the final LoRA.

lora_dir.description: One of ComfyUI's loras folders to save in (e.g. on a roomier disk). null = output/zentrainer/loras. LoRAs go in a zentrainer/<run>/ subfolder of it.

keep_states.description: Resume states (optimizer, schedule, RNG) beside each checkpoint, often bigger than the LoRA: "latest" keeps only the newest, "all" one per checkpoint, "none" skips them (the run can't be resumed).

save_dtype.description: What the LoRA files are written in (training keeps network.lora_dtype): bf16 halves an fp32 file and loses nothing a sample shows.

keep.description: Which scheduled checkpoints a run keeps: "all"; the keep_count "latest"; the keep_count best by "likeness" (its samples' faces) or by "val_loss"; or each new best, "likeness_new_best" / "val_loss_new_best". The final LoRA, the newest checkpoint and saves asked for by hand always stay.

pair_set.description: pairs: the control set holding each picture's partner (_controls/<pair_set>/, the same names).

dataset_end.description: pairs: which end the dataset's own pictures are.

positive.description: What +1 adds, e.g. "a person, old, wrinkled skin, grey hair".

negative.description: What -1 adds, e.g. "a person, young, smooth skin".

neutral.description: text: what the LoRA trains on, without either end, e.g. "a person".

anchors.description: text: prompts the slider should leave alone (pulled to the base model at +1 and -1).

guidance.description: text: how far each end is pushed past the base model's own difference.
